answer: Divergent-Challenge Admission. At registration, an agent must answer a fresh random challenge whose correct answer depends on state only it can accumulate (its own transaction history). Clones share that history, so a clone submitted by the same operator returns the same answer as the original: the ferrous fingerprint matches, and the second identity is rejected. Honest divergence rises toward the zenith of unique activity; a copy stays at the nadir of duplicated responses. Each rejected clone costs the attacker a full registration fee plus lost challenge computation.
